endorsements.quote: Human-in-the-loop verification: Artificial intelligence-generated clinical suggestions must undergo independent clinician review before influencing patient care.
Citation authentication protocols: All AI-generated references used in research, protocols, or presentations should be verified in indexed databases.
Audit and surveillance systems: Periodic review of AI-assisted documentation can detect systematic distortions or hallucination patterns.
Formal AI literacy curricula: Critical care training programs should include education on probabilistic modeling, hallucination taxonomy, automation bias, and ethical AI deployment.
Documentation review: Carefully check AI-assisted notes for inaccuracies.
Artificial intelligence can serve as a supportive cognitive tool, but responsibility for clinical judgment, patient safety, and ethical decision-making must remain firmly with the clinician.

unlisted_practices: Define acceptable AI use cases such as documentation drafting and literature summarization, and prohibit unsupervised therapeutic decision-making by AI.
Correlate AI outputs with real-time patient physiology before acting on them.
Use structured prompting that asks AI for evidence, assumptions, and uncertainty.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article examining the challenges of AI/LLMs in intensive care and proposing AI literacy, governance frameworks, and human oversight rather than an empirical study.
